label: GitHub
description: PR commands in M-p, the PRs view, PR numbers and merge states in tabs and the Work map; off, the workspace asks GitHub nothing by itself (programs you run, such as codex-review and wtpr, still do)

label: Linear
description: Ticket commands in M-p, ticket titles in tab names and tickets in the Work map; off, the workspace asks Linear nothing by itself (programs you run, such as wt and worktree-done, still do)

label: Cache PR and ticket images
description: Keeps the pictures, stylesheet, scripts and drawn pages of the PR and ticket image views on this computer, up to 300 MB, so one opened again shows at once; off, everything is fetched and drawn each time

label: Push notifications
description: A desktop notification, named for the tab, when a Claude tab waits on you

label: Finished tabs clear
description: When a tab's finished mark goes: once you look at the tab, or only when you next prompt it

label: UX 2.0
description: No status line: each tab has a header naming it, with the keys of what it can show in Claude's place (M-c Claude, M-d Diff, M-v PR, M-i Ticket, M-e Note); the sidebar starts with its notifications; M-v and M-i show the PR and the ticket in Claude's place rather than beside it, laid out as their pages are with a panel of their facts beside the description; and M-d's diff reads as one scroll of files under its story's chapters, the chapter's why over the diff and each hunk's note in a card under it. Off, the status line, the sidebar and those keys are as before

label: Sidebar
description: The sidebar on the left of every window; M-s still hides or shows it for now

label: Shade the sidebar
description: The sidebar is drawn on a shade of its own, a step darker than the panes, as UX 2.0's canvas draws it; off, it is drawn on the terminal's background as before. The chosen row keeps its shade and accent bar either way

label: Half-page scrolling
description: C-d and C-u in the sidebar, and the wheel over it, scroll its list half a screen down or up, the cursor moving with it, as in Vim, one flick of the wheel moving once; off, C-d and C-u run in the chosen tab as other Ctrl keys do and the wheel moves a tab at a time

label: Sidebar repository filter
description: M-p's Filter the sidebar to a repository moves every other repository's tabs to an Other repos group at the bottom, whatever they are doing, until Show every repository's tabs clears it; the filter is kept across restarts. Off, the commands are gone and every tab is in its own group

label: Select several tabs
description: v in the sidebar, or a Shift-click on a tab, selects several tabs to close at once from one menu. Off, v does nothing, a Shift-click on a tab goes there as a click does, and the sidebar acts on one tab at a time

label: Reminders
description: M-p's Remind me about this tab: the tab waits under Reminders with the time left, then moves to Needs you with a banner when it comes due, and mission control's Reminders view shows every tab's reminder, on a month with UX 2.0; off, reminders are neither set nor shown, and the view is gone

label: Reminders in the sidebar
description: Tabs waiting on a reminder sit under Reminders in the sidebar. Off, they are left out of the sidebar, the top line counts them (⏰ 3) and a click there opens mission control's Reminders view; a tab comes back under Needs you when its reminder comes due

label: Build failing
description: A Build failing group in the sidebar and mission control for the tabs whose open PR has a failing check, asked of GitHub every minute, an idle one wearing a red ✗; off, they stay in Working or Idle with the failing count in their words #github

label: Show the landing queue
description: Tabs landing on the default branch with queue-and-clean, or waiting their turn, get a Landing group in the sidebar and mission control, in the landing queue's order, which a waiting tab's menu changes; off, they show as Working, and the queue still orders the landings

label: Autopilot
description: With it on, M-p's 'Autopilot: work a note' keeps tabs working through a note's checklist, opening the next item with wtn as each lands; the mode itself starts off until you turn it on there. Off, it opens no tabs, and its line in mission control and its notification go

label: Close a worked note's landed tabs
description: When a tab autopilot opened closes once queue-and-clean has landed it and moved it back to the main clone: when seen, as soon as you leave it after seeing it, or 30 minutes after landing if you never look; at once, as soon as it lands; after 5 minutes, or sooner once seen and left; never, left open for you to close. Whatever the choice, a tab in front stays until you leave it and a prompt typed in it after landing keeps it open; one closed without being seen leaves a notification while Notify when autopilot lands is on

label: Autopilot's hands-free mode
description: Lets autopilot's menu offer 'Hands-free', which has its tabs take the recommended option of what they would ask you (a question box, a question that ends the turn, an item whose plan needs a choice), write each decision into the item's plan as a 'Decided hands-free' line, and land without asking; what your rules or a skill say must be asked still asks. The mode itself starts off. Off, the menu doesn't offer it and every tab asks as usual

label: Notify when autopilot lands
description: Puts each item autopilot lands without asking, and each landed tab it closes before you saw it, in the sidebar's notifications and the Slack relay's main DM. Off, they show only in the Autopilot view's Landed column, the Notifications view's history (as dismissed) and the item's Done: line

label: Keep opening tabs while I'm away
description: Autopilot keeps opening tabs for the note's next items while you're away (the screen locked, or no input for 10 minutes), up to its slots, most tabs open and spend limit, so it works through the note overnight with a terminal attached. Off, it opens nothing while you're away and finishes only the tabs already open

label: Autopilot's push allowed in auto mode
description: A tab autopilot opens in a repository that lands straight on a branch starts its Claude with the landing's one push, git push origin HEAD:<branch>, allowed for that session, so Claude Code's auto mode doesn't refuse it; every other push and tab still asks. Off, the push is judged as any command is, and a tab landing without asking may stop at it

label: Watch the default branch's CI
description: While autopilot works on a repository, or a tab waits to land on it, and its landings test in CI, Switchboard looks at its default branch's CI every two minutes and tells you when it fails, naming the commit and the line of the log that says why. Off, nothing looks, and you hear of a failing default branch only from the next landing

label: Keep the computer awake while tabs work
description: While a tab's Claude works (background work and watches too, not a /loop between its runs) or autopilot, on and not paused, has tabs open, the computer doesn't sleep when idle (caffeinate on macOS, a logind inhibitor on Linux), shown by a ☕ on the status line, or with UX 2.0 at the top of the sidebar; it lets go two minutes after everything is idle, the display still sleeps, and a laptop closed with no display on it sleeps anyway. M-p's 'Keep the computer awake until I say' holds it whatever runs. Off, the computer sleeps on its own schedule unless held from M-p

label: Notifications
description: The Notifications block at the bottom of the sidebar: new Slack messages and your Linear inbox, which a click opens in mission control

label: Notifications' history
description: Mission control's Notifications view keeps every notification of the last two weeks by day, with what each led to and whether the sidebar still shows it, in ~/.local/state/switchboard/notifications on this computer; off, the view shows only the sidebar's notifications, as they are now, and nothing is kept

label: PR notifications
description: The sidebar tells you when one of your PRs merges, is approved or its checks start failing, from the PRs board's lookups; off, it doesn't

label: M-a goes to notifications
description: M-a's walk of what needs you ends at the notifications while there are any, after the tabs, opening them as the sidebar's n does

label: Notifications window
description: Moving the sidebar's cursor onto a notification, or clicking one, brings the Notifications window to the front as moving onto a tab does: a tab of its own listing every one with its whole message, Enter opening its menu and Esc going back, which M-p's "Go to the notifications" brings to the front too; off, Enter or a click on one in the sidebar does what it leads to

label: New notes
description: In the sidebar's notifications, a note written for you (a meeting's from Fathom, the standup) until you read it, Enter offering to open it in Notes

label: Next meeting
description: In the sidebar's notifications, from five minutes before a meeting until ten after it starts: its name, the tickets and PRs it mentions, and Enter or a click to join its call

label: Docs in the link view
description: The link view reads a Notion page or a Google Doc or Slides deck through Claude's connectors, a headless Haiku fetching it; off, they are read as any other page, which a private one won't let it

label: Chrome profiles
description: Links Switchboard opens (mission control, the link view, M-r, M-l, switchboard open-url) open in the Chrome profile browser.json gives their site, else its default profile; off, every link opens in the default browser

label: Standup note
description: Each weekday from 6am, a note in Standups written from the last working day: the PRs you merged, opened, worked on and reviewed, your tickets that changed state and your commits, then what is in progress today and the reviews waiting on you

label: Standup summary
description: Over the standup note's list of the last working day, two or three sentences summing it up, written by Claude (Haiku, no tools) from the PR, ticket and commit titles in that list

label: Today's todo note
description: Each weekday at the time below, a note Todos/Today's Todo <date> that Claude (Sonnet) writes from your notes' unticked items, today's calendar, and what mission control last read of GitHub, Linear and Slack; off by default, since it sends your notes' unticked items to Claude

label: Todo note time
description: When Today's todo note is written each weekday, or as soon as the computer is on after it

label: Meeting notes
description: Each meeting of yours Fathom recorded as a note in Meetings, with its summary, action items and transcript, through Claude's Fathom connector (a Haiku call every 30 minutes from 7am to 9pm, and two for each new meeting)

label: Search everything
description: M-S-f asks for a search and lists what your notes, Linear, GitHub and Slack hold for it, each read beside the pane with Enter

label: Slack in search everything
description: M-S-f searches Slack too, through Claude's connector, a headless Haiku making that one call, its results arriving a few seconds after the others

label: Files in reading order
description: M-d lists the changed files flat, documentation first and tests last, with Haiku ordering the code from most abstract to most concrete; off, flat, A to Z

label: Diff told as a story
description: M-d's file list grouped into a few chapters Haiku names from the whole diff and the commits' messages, each with a heading and two or three sentences on what it does and why it is built so, read from the change's core to its edges ([c and ]c move between them, yS copies the story as Markdown); off, the files keep the reading order by kind. Sends the diff's text and the commit messages, not only the paths, to Claude

label: Click in menus
description: A click takes an option of mission control's menus, Yes or No of a question or a numbered answer, and a click outside the box closes it; a right click on an item in mission control, the Notifications window or the sidebar opens its menu, and where no item is the view's (the sidebar's own in the sidebar); and a click picks an option of M-m's, the update box's and M-w's menus; off, they take keys alone

label: Notifications hand off to a tab
description: Every notification's menu, and the Slack, Inbox, Calendar and Autopilot views' and a failing default branch's in the CI view, offers Send it to a tab, which pastes its words and link into the Claude of a tab you pick without sending, and Open a tab for it, which starts a tab with Claude told about it (a failing default branch's in its repository's main clone, told to fix it). Off, the menus keep their own choices only

label: Open boxes by the click
description: A menu or question a click opens appears beside the place clicked, so its options are a short move away; one opened by a key stays in the middle. Off, every box opens in the middle of the screen

label: Tab moves focus
description: Tab and Shift-Tab move a highlight through what can be clicked, as on a webpage, and Enter presses it (Space too, but in the sidebar, where Space peeks): in mission control the views' names, the filter and the items, with [ ] switching views; in the sidebar each of its rows, M-Space opening mission control; and the options of every box and menu; off, Tab switches views in mission control and opens it from the sidebar

label: Highlight on hover
description: What a click would press lights under the mouse: in mission control the views' names, the filter, the cards and rows, a menu's options, Yes and No, an answer's options and easy mode's ×; the sidebar's tabs and notifications; the options of M-m's, the update box's and M-w's menus; and the buttons of Notes' toolbar, its boxes' × and M-d's diff. In Ghostty and kitty the mouse pointer also turns into a hand over what a click presses (the workspace's sidebar, header, status line, mission control and boxes) and a resizing arrow over a line between panes. Off, nothing follows the mouse and the pointer is never changed. Takes effect at once in mission control and the sidebar, and when a menu, Notes or the diff next opens

label: Diff story progress
description: While M-d's story is told, its cover shows what Haiku is reading, each chapter as Haiku names it and the time taken, t showing Haiku's answer itself as it comes; off, a spinner alone

label: Diff story told ahead
description: When a tab's branch has a new commit, its M-d story is told in the background, so M-d opens on it at once rather than waiting under its cover; sends that branch's diff and commit messages to Claude (Haiku) for each new commit, a run taking up to five and a half minutes

label: Uncommitted changes in M-d
description: M-d's diff runs from the PR's base to the working tree, marking files with changes not yet committed and listing them in a last chapter; off, it shows the branch's commits only

label: Diff file list wide
description: M-d's file list opens wide enough for its longest path (at most half the screen), E narrowing it; off, it opens narrow and E widens it

label: Diff story a page at a time
description: ]p and [p in M-d's diff open the story's chapters one at a time, each a diff of its own as if it were a commit, [p from the first going back to the whole diff; off, they do nothing

label: Ask Claude about the diff
description: ga in M-d's diff, and M-p's command while the diff is open, ask Haiku a question about the change: it reads the story, the diff and where the cursor is, and may read the repository's files to answer, its answer streamed into a window beside the diff. Sends the diff and the question to Claude

label: Ask in the tab's session
description: With Ask Claude about the diff on, ga asks a copy of the tab's own Claude session, which knows the conversation that made the change, on that session's model; the tab's conversation is left as it was, and Haiku answers in its place when the session can't be resumed. Off, it asks a fresh Haiku with the story and the diff alone, which costs less

label: Diff story notes on changes
description: M-d's diff shows Haiku's note over each change worth one, what it does and what to check, and names the chapter of a change that belongs to another one than its file; off, only the list's chapters

label: Summaries of each turn
description: With UX 2.0, each card says what its tab's last turn did, in a sentence Haiku writes as the turn ends from the turn's prompt and last reply, which this sends to Claude; off, as it is by default, nothing is sent and a card shows the reply's first line

label: Work map
description: Mission control's Work map: every piece of work in your tabs' repositories (M-j and M-o open it whatever this says)

label: Calendar
description: Mission control's Calendar view: today from the day /today last saved

label: Slack
description: Mission control's Slack view: your mentions, DMs, thread replies and chosen channels from the last day, as /slack-updates saved them

label: Closed tabs
description: Mission control's Closed view: the tabs closed last, to reopen

label: Sessions
description: Mission control's Sessions view: each Claude session's context, model and age

label: Resources
description: Mission control's Resources view: the computer's CPU and memory, and a table of the CPU and memory each tab's processes use, sorted by CPU or memory, read from the kernel every few seconds only while the view is in front; with UX 2.0 a board of sparklines and each tab's process tree, whose menu can end a process. Off, the view and its readings are gone

label: Requests in Usage
description: The Usage view lists today's requests to services outside this computer (GitHub, Linear, Slack, Anthropic and the rest), by protocol and by service, as Switchboard counts them; off, it leaves them out

label: Usage
description: Mission control's Usage view: today's Claude spend and how much of the rate limits is used

label: Keys
description: Mission control's Keys view, which M-/ opens: every key Switchboard binds, the workspace's grouped by their first tag, then the sidebar's, mission control's, M-d's and Notes', then the commands reached only through M-p, with / to filter, Enter's menu to press a workspace key and m's to find a key by pressing it; with UX 2.0, a board with a heatmap of the Alt keys you pressed this week (counted with habits on); off, M-/ reaches the pane

label: M-A cycles idle tabs
description: M-A goes to the next idle tab, in the sidebar's Idle order, wrapping at the end, as M-a walks the tabs that need you; off, M-A reaches the pane

label: Tab history
description: M-h shows a tab's history: its Claude session on a timeline (its state, your turns, commits, review rounds and context) under its screen as it was at the moment you move to, the screens kept in the server's memory only, never on disk, and the rest read from the session's transcript; off, nothing is kept, M-h says it is off and the header has no History key

label: Tab age and stage times
description: Shows how long each tab has been open, as 'opened 1h12m' in the UX 2.0 tab header and on mission control's cards, and how long each stage of an autopilot tab took (or has taken so far) on its board; off, none of them is shown, while a landed item's Done line still says how long it took, since the landing writes it

label: Widest a lone pane gets
description: A tab with one pane (or zoomed into one), and mission control showing one view, is drawn at most this wide, against the sidebar, its program given that width and the columns at its right the sidebar's sunken surface with a rule at the pane's right edge; with two or more panes they share the whole width and may be wider, and several views at once fill it too. Off, a lone pane fills the width

label: M-[ and M-] go back and forward
description: M-[ and M-] go back and forward through the tabs you visited, as a browser's back and forward do, and do nothing with nowhere further to go; off, they go to the tab on the left and right, as the prefix's p and n always do

label: One Claude to a tab
description: A Claude session started in a tab already running one moves to a tab of its own, since the sidebar, the Slack relay, M-c and M-m each take a tab's Claude to be one pane

label: Name new tabs
description: M-t and M-n ask what to call the tab they open: a name typed in, its ticket and the ticket's title, or shaping a ticket, each optional; off, the tab is named after its directory

label: Messages in a box
description: What a key or script has to say shows in a small box in the middle of the screen, which any key closes, rather than on the status line for a moment

label: Opening-link message
description: Opening a link says where it is going (the site, Chrome and its profile) in a box until the browser comes to the front, since a profile's Chrome can take seconds to start. Off, links open with nothing said

label: Calendar changes
description: In the sidebar's notifications, what changed on today's calendar since you last looked at it: an event added, moved, renamed or gone; looking at the Calendar view clears them

label: Hide the sidebar beside a tab
description: When M-e brings Notes beside another tab's pane, put the notes app's sidebar away so the note has the room, and show it again in Notes' own tab

label: Notes command palette
description: M-p with Notes in front lists every command Notes has, each with its key, ahead of the workspace's, as Ctrl-Shift-P does in Notes run alone; off, M-p leaves them out and Ctrl-Shift-P in Notes run alone says the palette is off

label: Ctrl-V pastes an image
description: Ctrl-V while typing in a note pastes the clipboard's image under the line, as in Claude Code, when the clipboard holds one; off, or with no image there, Ctrl-V types the next key as it is, as in Vim

label: Images drawn in a note
description: An image pasted into a note (Format menu, Paste image) drawn under the line that names it, in a terminal that speaks the kitty graphics protocol (Ghostty and kitty do), or one that draws sixel with Image protocol on sixel (Windows Terminal); off, it is its name, which Enter opens as "Enter shows a picture full size" says

label: Chips on checklist items
description: With UX 2.0 on, each checklist item shows at its right the tab working on it (its number in the tab's color, a click going there), "landed <hash>" once ticked with its commit named under it, "plan" where it links its plan (a click opening it) and "needs a choice" while one waits, its text cut with … before them except on the cursor's line; off, items are their text alone

label: Enter shows a picture full size
description: Enter or a click on a note's picture shows it full size over the notes pane, as it does a picture or diagram under the cursor in the PR, ticket, link and file views, drawn by the workspace in a terminal that speaks the kitty graphics protocol (Ghostty, kitty) with "Images in the workspace" on, Esc going back; off, or where the terminal can't, it opens in Quick Look or the desktop's image viewer

label: Toolbar
description: A row of buttons over each note, one for each of the Format menu's styles (bold, italic, headings, lists, checklist, table, link, image) and ⋯ for the whole menu, each acting on the line or the selection; off, the Format menu is Ctrl-P alone

label: Tell a note's new tab its note
description: A new tab opened for a note from Notes starts Claude knowing the note's title and file (added to its system prompt, no turn spent), to read when you ask, or first while Point Claude at the tab's note is on; off, it starts as any other tab

label: wtpr asks where the PR stands
description: Claude, started in a PR's worktree by wtpr (or mission control's "work on it in a new tab"), first reads the PR, its review threads, failing checks and ticket and says where it stands and what it would do next, changing nothing until you say; off, it starts with no prompt

label: Notes beside a note's tab
description: Opening a note's tab from Notes (t, or M-p's Open the tab for the note) moves Notes beside the tab's Claude showing the note, as M-e does; off, it only goes to the tab

label: Show a note's item whole in wtn's list
description: M-p's "Start work on a note's checklist items" shows the item under the cursor whole in the lower half of its list, its full text and what is indented under it, since the list cuts each item to one line; off, the list has the whole box

label: Ask for a tab's note
description: When M-e brings Notes beside a tab with no note of its own yet, ask which note is the tab's, the likely ones first, and show that note beside it from then on

label: M-e opens the tab's plan or autopilot's note
description: M-e shows the note you linked to the tab, else the plan of an autopilot tab's item, else the note autopilot is working through, else the note shown there last. Off, M-e shows the tab's note or the one shown there last, as before.

label: Point Claude at the tab's note
description: As a Claude session starts in a tab with a note of its own, tell it the note's path and to read it before its first reply, so the note's standing rules reach every session in the tab, in any repository, while Switchboard loads as a plugin (claude_plugin), whose session-start hook does it; off, a session reads the note only when asked to. Off by default, since it has Claude read a note on its own

label: RSVP from the Calendar
description: Answer an invitation yes, maybe or no from its Enter menu in the Calendar view, through Claude's Google Calendar connector

label: Attendees' photos in the Calendar
description: Show the photos of who is going to the Calendar view's chosen event, looked up by each attendee's email address in Linear and the Slack relay's app (users:read.email), which sends those addresses to them. Off, as it is by default, no address is sent and each attendee is their initial

label: Slack without a tab
description: Mission control looks at Slack itself every minute, through cheap headless Haiku calls, instead of a Slack tab looping /slack-updates

label: Slack threads and pictures
description: With UX 2.0, the Slack view shows the chosen message's whole thread beside it, with its pictures and videos, which each look reads through Claude's Slack connector (a few more headless Haiku calls a look) and keeps on this computer; off, the view lists the messages alone and reads no threads or files

label: Pause lookups while away
description: Stop asking GitHub, Linear and the calendar for mission control's views, and telling the diff's stories ahead, while no terminal is attached, or the computer has been locked, or idle 10 minutes, with no key pressed in Switchboard since (from another computer over SSH too), and catch up on return

label: Look often
description: Ask GitHub and Linear every 15 seconds (the PR board every 30) and look at the Slack Home tab every 10, in place of every one or two minutes: about eight times as many requests, which can reach GitHub's 5,000 an hour

label: PR board
description: Mission control's PRs view, which asks GitHub about your pull requests every two minutes

label: Ticket board
description: Mission control's Tickets view, which asks Linear about the issues assigned to you every two minutes

label: Inbox
description: Mission control's Inbox view and the sidebar's count of it: your unread Linear mentions, comments and assignments, asked of Linear every two minutes #linear

label: CI
description: Mission control's CI view: your pull requests failing, running and passing, each failed check with the line of its log that says why and, with UX 2.0, its failing step beside the list, asked of GitHub every two minutes #github

label: Landing view
description: While a tab is landing or waiting to land, mission control shows each repository's landing queue or merge queue (everyone's PRs in it, asked of GitHub every 15 seconds), in queue order, with the tab that has each; a waiting one's menu moves it or takes it out

label: Routines
description: Prompts of yours on a schedule, each run in a Claude tab of its own, and the Routines view in mission control; off, no routine runs and the view is gone, the routines kept

label: Autopilot view
description: With UX 2.0 on, while autopilot works a note, mission control shows a view of it: the note, its tabs working and open against its slots and cap, today's spend against its limit, and a board of every item it works, a card in the column where it stands (Next up, Working, Waiting on you, Landing, Landed, Skipped). Off, its line above the tabs stays and the view goes; on, the view takes the line's place

label: Second status line
description: The line under the tabs with the tab's name, branch, PR and Claude session

label: PRs and tickets in tab names
description: Look up each tab's PR number on GitHub and its ticket's title on Linear, in the background

label: Project colors
description: A color of its own for each project's tab, made from its directory; off, every tab is gray

label: Tab colors
description: The colors tabs take from their project, in the tab bar, the sidebar, the header and Claude's statusline: soft pastels, as the UX 2.0 canvas draws them, or the stronger colors from before. Each tab keeps its own hue either way

label: A color a tab
description: Each tab gets the hue farthest from the open tabs' as it opens, a deeper shade of it when it is close to one, kept while it is open and through restarts, so tabs, and the Usage view's spend chart, tell apart. Off, a tab wears its directory's color, the same for every tab of one checkout

label: Health light
description: A red mark in the status bar when saves, the sidebar or the Slack relay quietly stop

label: Images in the workspace
description: Draws avatars, pictures, meters, charts and the shadow under boxes as images where the terminal can show them (Ghostty, kitty). Off, they are drawn with characters

label: Scroll bars
description: A scroll bar at the right of every list, view and pane with more than fits, showing where you are: a click on its track pages toward the click, and dragging its thumb scrolls with it. Off, nothing is drawn there

label: People's photos
description: Avatars show people's photos from Slack (through the Slack relay's app, with the users:read scope), Linear and GitHub, and, with calendar_photos on, calendar attendees' by their address, each fetched once and kept in ~/.cache/switchboard/photos for 30 days. Off, nothing is fetched and an avatar is the person's initial

label: Pictures and diagrams in the views
description: Draws the pictures on lines of their own and the Mermaid diagrams in the PR, ticket, link and file views as images where the terminal can show them (Ghostty, kitty), fetching the pictures and drawing the diagrams with Mermaid in Chrome, and draws the diagrams of the description beside mission control's PR and ticket boards the same way (with "Images in the workspace" on too). Off, a picture is its name and a diagram is drawn with characters

label: A cursor in the views
description: Gives the PR, ticket, link and file views a cursor, a yellow › that j and k move from line to line, a picture or diagram one step, the screen scrolling to keep it in sight; Enter or a click on a picture or diagram shows it full size over the view, as a note's does, Esc going back. Off, the views scroll as less does, and a click on a picture opens its link

label: Theme
description: The status line's, the pane borders' and the boxes' colors, dark drawn in the UX 2.0 canvas's colors on a terminal that shows truecolor and in the 256-color palette elsewhere; system follows the terminal's own background, which it is asked for as it attaches

label: Set the terminal's colors
description: While Switchboard is attached, sets your terminal's background and text colors to the dark theme's, so the padding around the window matches; puts the terminal's own back when you detach. Off, the terminal keeps its own colors.

label: Image protocol
description: How pictures (a note's images, the PR and ticket image views) reach your terminal: kitty passes kitty's graphics commands on, for Ghostty and kitty; sixel has the workspace draw each picture itself as sixel where it shows, for a terminal that draws sixel but not kitty's pictures, as Windows Terminal (1.22 and later) does; Notes and the image view opened after a change draw by it

label: Copy Claude's reply
description: M-y copies the latest reply of the tab's Claude to the clipboard, read from its session transcript; off, the key reaches the pane

label: Log Claude's hooks
description: Write a line to the server's log (server.log in Switchboard's state directory) for each hook Claude Code runs in a pane: the event, the tool, the pane, the call's id, the subagent and a notification's kind, never what was asked or run; for finding out why a tab showed the wrong state. Off, nothing is logged

label: Show a tab's full title
description: M-T, the sidebar's i and a tab's menu in mission control show the tab's whole title in a box, with its branch, directory, PR and ticket, which the sidebar and the status line cut; off, the key reaches the pane

label: Save what panes show
description: Keep each pane's screen in the layout saves, to show again after a restart; it can hold secrets

label: Offer to apply a landed change
description: After queue-and-clean lands work, it lists what the change needs to take effect (Switchboard built and put in place, the Slack relay restarted, an install, a migration) and offers to do it

label: Restore on start
description: Bring back the last saved tabs and panes, each Claude resumed, when the server starts with none open

label: Load Switchboard as a plugin
description: Claude in Switchboard's panes loads its hooks (the tabs' Claude states), skills and instructions as a plugin, and setup keeps them out of ~/.claude, so Claude elsewhere has only your own; it needs Claude Code 2.1.280 or later, and managed settings that don't set disableSideloadFlags. Off, setup puts them in ~/.claude as before, for every Claude of yours. Changing it moves them over

label: Context in Claude's status line
description: Claude Code's status line under its prompt says how full the context is, beside the model, inside the workspace as outside it. Off, with UX 2.0 and mission control's Sessions view on, the status line inside the workspace shows the model alone and the Sessions view shows the context; without both of those it shows the context anyway

label: Rules in reviews
description: codex-review gives the reviewer the repository's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md as the base has them and your own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with what it imports, and reports a change that breaks one; off, it reviews without them, and your rules aren't sent to the reviewer

label: Review before pushing
description: In this repository, a push to main needs a clean /review-loop first (.githooks/pre-push); off, it pushes without one

label: Learn from what you pick
description: M-p remembers what you typed before each pick, and puts that command first when you type the same again

label: Links you gave Claude
description: M-p's link commands also list the links in what you sent the pane's Claude, pasted text included, which Claude Code doesn't show. Off, they list only what the pane shows

label: Commands button
description: A ⌘ Commands button that opens M-p when clicked: in the status bar after the session name, or with UX 2.0 at the right end of the tab header's keys, where a click while the palette is open closes it

label: Security review in the review loop
description: /review-loop runs Claude Code's /security-review on the branch once before its first round, its findings fixed or asked about as the rounds' are

label: Ask before closing a pane
description: M-w asks first when a program runs in the pane (a shell at its prompt closes at once); off, it closes the pane at once whatever runs in it

label: Tips
description: A box in the top-right corner, once each, when a key would help (M-a, M-j, putting a pane back); any key closes it

label: Suggestions from how you work
description: Count the keys you press, the commands you pick in M-p and the mission control views you open, on this computer only and never sent anywhere, and suggest in the notifications a view to turn off that you never open, a key for a command you keep picking in M-p, or a feature that is off which what you do would use; off, what was counted is removed

label: Easy mode
description: Keys for people who don't know Vim's, in Notes and M-d's diff: Shift-arrows and the mouse select, typing replaces a selection, Cmd-S saves, Cmd-Z undoes, Cmd-Shift-Z redoes and Cmd-X cuts in a note (where the terminal sends them as the guide says), and the diff gets a row of buttons for its keys; mission control's boxes, M-m's, the update box's and M-w's menus, messages, tips, and Notes' Format menu, palette and finder get a × in their top-right corner that a click or Tab and Enter closes, with Click in menus on (lists to pick from, such as M-p's, keep Esc alone); Vim's keys keep working. Takes effect when Notes or the diff next opens

label: Key help line
description: With Easy mode on, a line at the bottom of Notes and M-d's diff naming the keys that work there

label: Alt-arrows move between panes
description: M-Left, M-Right, M-Up and M-Down move to the pane on that side, as C-w h, l, k and j do in Vim; off, they reach the pane

label: Resize the pane beside a board
description: In mission control, the pane resize keys (C-M-S-h and C-M-S-l) and a drag of its left edge widen or narrow the pane beside the PRs, Tickets and Autopilot boards, each board keeping its width. Off, the pane keeps its share of the screen and the keys and its edge do nothing there

label: C-w then h, j, k or l moves between panes
description: C-w followed by h, j, k or l moves to the pane on that side, as in Vim, which itself still gets C-w; C-w twice sends one to the pane. In mission control, C-w and h or l move between a view's side panel, list and the pane beside it. Off, C-w reaches the pane as it is, deleting a word in a shell or Claude's prompt, and a mission control view's list keeps the keys

label: Extended keys
description: Your terminal is asked to tell keys such as Ctrl-Shift-P from Ctrl-P and Shift-Enter from Enter, as tmux's extended-keys did, and a program that asks for them (Notes, Neovim, the kitty keyboard protocol's) gets them so, while the rest get the keys as before; off, every key reaches every program as a plain terminal sends it. Takes effect when a terminal next attaches and for panes opened after

label: Update check
description: Offer a new release of Switchboard: when a terminal attaches and every hour, only when one attaches, or never

label: Offer to restart after an update
description: Once switchboard update has put a new release in place, ask whether to restart the workspace on it now, keeping every tab and what runs in it; off, it only says how (switchboard upgrade)

label: Build before restarting
description: M-p's "Restart Switchboard on the latest build on disk" first brings the main clone of the checkout a build from a clone came from up to date with origin, on its default branch with nothing uncommitted, and builds it (cargo build --release --locked; a try builds its worktree) and puts it in place of the binary the server runs, restarting only when that is new (from a cargo target directory, which other worktrees write over, the build goes to ~/.local/bin/switchboard, else a copy in ~/.cache/switchboard/build, and the restart runs from there); off, it restarts on the binary on disk as it is, when that is new

label: Skills and instructions from the clone
description: A build made from a clone reads its skills, Claude settings, instructions and settings list from that clone's assets/ folder, so a change there is live once it lands: the plugin and the parts you set up are brought up to date within seconds, with no rebuild or restart. A release build has no clone and keeps what it carries. Off, every build uses what it carries

label: Haiku summaries
description: One line on what each tab is doing in the relay's Home tab and progress, each a paid Haiku call

label: Ask before typing over a draft
description: A message sent to a tab from Slack while text is typed and unsent in its prompt waits, and the thread asks whether to replace the draft, send after it or keep it. Off, the message is typed after whatever is there and sent, as before

label: Close the relay's tab when it stops
description: Stopping the Slack relay, from M-p, `slack-relay stop`, `stop` in its DM or Ctrl-C in its tab, closes its tab; a crash or a start it refuses keeps the tab at a shell with the error. Off, the tab stays at a shell whenever the relay ends

label: Reminder tabs on the Slack Home
description: Lists the tabs under the sidebar's Reminders on the Slack app's Home too, each saying when it reminds you. Off, they are left out until their reminder comes due, and the Home says how many
